paper.title: Structure-aware graph neural network based deep transfer learning framework for enhanced predictive analytics on diverse materials datasets
paper.research_summary: This paper presents a structure-aware graph neural network (GNN) based deep transfer learning framework to improve predictive performance for materials properties using sparse data. It leverages the ALIGNN architecture trained on large source datasets (e.g., Materials Project formation energy) and applies transfer learning—via fine-tuning or feature extraction—to small target datasets across diverse materials classes (3D/2D, inorganic/organic, computational/experimental) and properties. Evaluation across 115 dataset-property combinations shows transfer learning models outperform scratch-trained models in ≈90% of cases, with particular gains for small datasets and extrapolation tasks.

tasks.objective: To accurately predict materials properties using crystal structure information, especially when training data is sparse.
output_goal: predicted numerical value of a target materials property

evidence.text: Here we present a framework for materials property prediction tasks using structure information that leverages graph neural network-based architecture along with deep-transfer-learning techniques to drastically improve the model’s predictive ability on diverse materials (3D/2D, inorganic/organic, computational/experimental) data.

stages.stage_goal: To collect a broad set of publicly available materials datasets covering diverse structures, classes, and properties.

evidence.text: We use nine datasets of DFT-computed and experimental properties in this work: Materials Project (MP)4, Joint Automated Repository for Various Integrated Simulations (JARVIS) 3D with 46 properties and 2D with 32 properties5, Flla44 with three properties, Dielectric Constant (DC)45 with five properties, Piezoelectric Tensor (PT)46 with two properties, Experimental Formation Energy (EFE)47 with one property, Kingsbury Experimental Formation Energy (KEFE)48 with one property, Kingsbury Experimental Bandgap (KEB)49 with one property, and Harvard Organic Photovoltaic Dataset (HOPV)50 with 24 properties.

stages.stage_name_raw: preprocessing of structure files into atom/bond/angle features
stages.stage_goal: To convert raw crystal structure files (e.g., POSCAR) into structured graph representations suitable for ALIGNN input.
stage_input: structure file containing information on lattice geometry and the ionic positions of a compound

evidence.text: The structure file containing information on lattice geometry and the ionic positions of a compound is divided into atom, bond, and angle-based features before feeding into the ALIGNN-based Feature Extractor where we perform feature extraction.

stages.stage_name_raw: training of source model (ALIGNN on MP formation energy)
stages.stage_goal: To train a robust, structure-aware source model on a large dataset (MP formation energy) to capture generalizable chemical and structural knowledge.

evidence.text: A model trained on the formation energy of the MP dataset39 is used as the source model to perform fine-tuning and feature extraction-based transfer learning as formation energy has shown to lead to meaningful representations from large source datasets36, which can then be applied during the model training on the smaller target datasets to improve their predictive performance.
We build source models using a structure-aware GNN-based architecture called ALIGNN on the MP dataset by using only formation energy as the source materials property.

stages.stage_name_raw: transfer learning via fine-tuning on target datasets
stages.stage_goal: To adapt the pre-trained ALIGNN source model to each target dataset by initializing weights from the source model and refining them on target data.

evidence.text: Fine-tuning uses the weights from the pre-trained model as the preliminary weight initialization for the network, which are further refined using the target dataset.

stages.stage_name_raw: feature extraction from pre-trained ALIGNN for target compounds
stages.stage_goal: To generate fixed-dimensional, structure-aware feature vectors (atom-bond-angle features) from the pre-trained ALIGNN model for each compound in the target dataset.
stage_output: 768-dimensional concatenated atom-bond-angle feature vector per compound

evidence.text: In the feature extraction method, we treat the pre-trained model as a feature extractor to extract robust features for the target dataset and use them to build the target model using representation learning.

In the feature extraction method, we treat the pre-trained model as the feature extractor and extract atom, bond, and angle-based features from a given layer, each containing a variable number of rows depending on the number of the atom, bond, and angle information present in the input file and 256 columns as features for each row.

stages.stage_name_raw: training of target model on extracted features
stages.stage_goal: To train a simple deep neural network (NN-17) on the extracted ALIGNN features to predict the target property.

evidence.text: Next, we perform model training using the above-defined set of features as input for the deep neural network where we use a 17-layered neural network comprising of stacks of fully connected layers and ReLU as the activation function inspired from21,22,55 as the base architecture and formation energy of JARVIS-3D dataset as the materials property for property prediction task, the results of which are shown in Table 1.

stages.stage_name_raw: evaluation of predictive performance using MAE
stages.stage_goal: To quantitatively assess and compare the accuracy of scratch-trained, fine-tuned, and feature-extraction-based models using mean absolute error (MAE) on holdout test sets.

evidence.text: We use mean absolute error (MAE) as the primary evaluation metric for all models.
Table 2 presents the prediction accuracy of the best SC and best TL model on the test set for each of the 48 target properties.
